newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strategie Grains sees large French feed wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Strategie Grains sees large French feed wheat crop.

text.p: French analyst Strategie Grains predicted on Monday that about half of France's 1997 soft wheat crop could end up in feed because of quality problems hitting milling wheat varieties.
In its report for August the analyst said that almost 17 million tonnes of soft wheat out of a total crop of 33.55 million tonnes could be destined for the feed industry.
The analyst however warned that the estimate drawn from data available up to August 11 must be taken with great caution as the harvest was not yet complete in northern France.
It also said that a joint ONIC/French crop quality institute (ITCF) grain quality survey expected for release in September would provide more details.
Strategie Grains data showed that some 30 percent of area was sown to feed wheat varieties in 1997 against 26 percent in 1996 and 19 percent in 1995.
This could have yielded a feed wheat crop of 11.710 million tonnes, with 21.840 million then available for milling.

But because of quality problems that hit the milling wheat varieties, France may end up with a larger than expected feed wheat crop of 16.670 million tonnes and a milling wheat crop of 16.880 million tonnes, the analyst said. The feed wheat figure could be revised upwards depending on the quality of the wheat not yet harvested in northern France, it said. The analyst explained that in some regions milling wheat varieties showed very weak Hagberg numbers and specific weights, that will make them unfit for bread-making.

"To date combining the results of each region and taking into account the quality problems of each variety, it seems that the production of wheat with a Hagberg of below 120 and a specific weight below 74...could be almost 17 million tonnes, that is about half the crop, and thus 15 percent more than if there had been no quality problems," it said.

Overall there were Hagberg problems south of the Loire river in regions where specific weights and protein contents were good. In the north specific weights were very weak, protein content satisfactory though lower than last year but there was no concern over Hagberg levels.
Strategie Grains put the 1997 soft wheat crop at 33.55 million tonnes against 34.70 million in 1996.
It put the barley crop at 10.05 million tonnes against 9.50 million in 1996.
The new barley total includes 7.07 million tonnes of winter barley and 2.98 million tonnes of spring barley.

Based on quality results up to August 11, the analyst predicted that at least some 2.84 million tonnes of barley could qualify for malting, up 20 percent over last year. This would include 1.2 million tonnes of winter barley and 1.64 million tonnes of spring barley.
